messages.body_plain:
-----BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE-----
Hash: SHA1


  I spent a little while cleaning up some problems with phylobase (the
version on CRAN looks broken -- I don't know how long it's been that
way).  It now passes checks on my machine with a couple of NOTEs, one
about the size of the 'libs' directory (which we can't really do
anything about), and one about redirection of output to stdout and
stderr, which is frowned upon.

There appear to be 34 instances of this in the C++ code:

grep  "\(cout\|cerr\)" *.cpp | wc
     34     563    3761

  Is someone willing to spend an hour or so figuring out how to
replace these appropriately?  (section 6.5 of the R-exts manual says
to use Rprintf and REprintf)  This has gone under the radar so far,
but I can imagine CRAN (who have been getting stricter and stricter)
will complain about this when we resubmit.

  This is with ape 3.0-6; as I said, it otherwise tests clean on my
machine, we'll see whether R-Forge complains or not.

  Volunteers?

   cheers
     Ben

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

  I'm currently in the field and won't have a chance to look into it until
early December. As I recall most (if not all) of these stdout/stderr are
actually remnants of the initial hack of NCL. The phylobase interface was
developed based on some example code provided with NCL that was a basic
command line parser of NEXUS files. From what I remember, most of these
stdout/stderr lines are not used by phylobase at all and could possibly be
removed without affecting the rest of the code.

  Cheers,
  -- Fran?ois

messages.body_plain:
I have been fussing with phylobase, and I think it's basically ready
to go, but I have a question for someone more knowledgeable than I am
about Nexus reading.

  We are getting a lot of warnings of this type:

 A TAXA block should be read before the TREES block (but no TAXA block
was found).  Taxa will be inferred from their usage in the TREES block.
at line 8, column (approximately) 9 (file position 217)
storing implied block: TAXA
storing read block: TREES

  you can look at tests/doRUnit.Rout.save to see examples.

  Can anyone say whether these are effectively false positives that
should be suppressed?

  cheers
    Ben

messages.subject: [Phylobase-devl] checking readNexus
messages.body_plain:
These warnings are generated by NCL as, by default, it only reads strictly
compliant NEXUS files which should include a TAXA block. However, we enable
the option to read "relaxed" NEXUS files that may omit the TAXA block which
generates the warnings. We might be able to silence them if needed. I don't
really have strong feelings either way.

  -- Fran?ois
